best_for: Arcade and retro computer fans on Windows or Linux who want one emulator for thousands of old machines, and who are comfortable sorting out their own ROM sets.
description:
MAME is an emulator built by the MAME development team, known as MAMEdev. The team treats it first as a reference on how each emulated machine worked inside. Being able to play the old software is, in their words, a welcome side effect that proves the emulation is faithful.

To run anything, you supply images of the original ROMs, CDs, hard disks or other media yourself. MAME ships with none of the original game code, and the team points out that these images are still under copyright, not abandonware. When you get stuck, the site offers the official documentation, guides for specific emulated systems, an FAQ, forums, GitHub Discussions and an IRC chat.

points.title: Far more than arcade games
points.text: MAME started as an arcade emulator and later absorbed the MESS project, so it now also covers vintage home computers, consoles and calculators. Its stated goal is preservation: the source code documents how the original hardware worked.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: The project as a whole is GPL-2.0, and more than 90% of its files, core included, are also under BSD-3-Clause. The MAME name and logo are trademarks, so forks cannot reuse them without permission.

points.title: Official binaries are Windows only
points.text: MAMEdev publishes 64-bit Windows packages for x64 and Arm64, plus source code. Other systems build from source or rely on packagers.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is a community build
points.text: The Flatpak listed here, for x64 and Arm64, is packaged on Flathub and is not verified by MAMEdev. Flathub marks its support as unknown.

points.title: No Mac download here
points.text: This page lists Windows and Linux only. Mac users have to build MAME from source or find a third-party package.

points.title: Releases have slowed
points.text: MAME used to ship almost every month. In April 2026 the team said releases would come less often, and 0.289 arrived on July 31, 2026, two months after 0.288.

points.title: Two Windows versions kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 2 versions and Linux lists only the current release, so older builds come from MAMEdev's own release archive.
